_field_contract: resume.sh does os.path.isdir(worktree) and git rev-list origin/<branch>..HEAD, so `worktree` and `branch` must each be ONE value. An agent working two repos records the other in second_worktree/second_branch, which resume.sh ignores. Writing 'a and b' there makes the next report say 'no worktree' for a worktree that is fine.

_findings.nft -c cannot run in a build container: netlink: Error: cache initialization failed: Operation not permitted. nft -c applies nothing, but libnftables opens a netlink socket and lists the LIVE ruleset before it will look at a file, and that needs CAP_NET_ADMIN over a real netns. The build had none, so the parser never ran and the step exited 1 at STEP 99/148. Fixed by giving it a netns of its own: unshare --user --map-root-user --net nft -c -f. Proved four ways with a fake unshare on PATH - parses / rejects a mutant at line 60 col 56-60 / unshare absent / unshare REFUSED - because the first draft classified unshare's own refusal as 'nft rejected the ruleset' and would have failed the build a second time on a false diagnosis.

_findings.root looked for every user's lid config: Merging the four rescued branches took the workspace to 588 passed / 1 failed, and the failure was a PRODUCT defect. owner_configs resolved another user's config path through the INVOKING process's XDG_CONFIG_HOME, so the uid scan - which is the path the root driver takes - looked for every user's lid config inside root's own XDG directory, and on any machine where that variable is set the owner's pin would have been ignored silently. It is also why the test passed alone and failed in a full run: a gaming.rs test sets XDG_CONFIG_HOME in the same process. Split into invoker_config_path and config_path_for_home; 2998 passed, 0 failed; restoring the single function reddens the test by name.

_findings.errexit does not apply to a `!`-inverted: THE defect class of round 21, and it invalidated three of my own fixes from the same day. bash(1) under `set -e` exempts 'any command in a pipeline but the last, or if the command's return value is being inverted with !'. So `set -e; ! grep -q x <<<x; echo REACHED` prints REACHED. Every `! grep` in these Containerfiles is written as a build-time refusal and 46 of them failed nothing — they are mid-stanza, so their status is discarded and the build only ever stops if some LATER command in the same RUN fails. Found by the p1-063 lid agent in its own stanza; it wrote its refusals as `if ... exit 1` from the start and that is the idiom adopted. Ten of the 46 are not greps and were never in reach of the resolver at all: `apex-mux nonsense-verb`, `apex vm create --graphics spice`, `apex secret --help`, `apex recover reset` as root, `command -v qemu-system-x86_64` — all carrying real security decisions and asserting nothing. Fixed in b1d1c5bf; the gate now reports a fourth number and exits 1 on it.
_findings.706489ec misdiagnosed what broke the bui: 706489ec's message says a bare `! grep -q '_keep'` 'failed on a correct file, and `set -eux` made that a failed image build'. It CANNOT have. `git show 5cb71ea0` puts all three polkit refusals in ONE commit with `<allow_inactive>yes` last, so the `_keep` line was mid-stanza from birth and never ran an exit status anybody read. The five-day breakage was the EFFECTIVE assertions: the nft check and the ApexShellKeybinds grep (neither inverted) and `mouse = true` (last in its stanza). Reasoned, not reproduced, by an agent with the same blind spot. Worth keeping as the lesson: a diagnosis written from a plausible mechanism inherits that mechanism's assumptions.

_findings.the assertion checker was skipping pipe-: It matched greps against physical LINES. A grep at the tail of a pipe looked like a grep with no file and was skipped with `continue` — not checked, and not counted as unchecked either, which is how it reported '0 failed' for 50 minutes while `apex-vm --help | grep` could never pass. A grep whose pattern and path sit on two lines — how this file writes every long one — looked identical. It now resolves from the joined top-level segments it already computes for the inert check: 98 checked -> 106, and unresolved rose to 154 because silent skips are finally visible. Both detectors re-proved against mutants after the refactor.

_findings.the Android unit has been wrong about th: Once fatally — correct worktrees code was deleted over a claim read off a validation-error enum. p1-053b closed the class by construction rather than by care: android/core/src/test/resources/requests.json is every request the app builds, asserted by Kotlin against the builders AND by apexd/apex-agent-core/tests/android_requests_wire.rs against Request's own serde. A verb that does not exist now fails to deserialize instead of being argued about. Two real defects also fixed: connecting to a second machine kept the first one's worktrees, grants and pending approvals; and replyToSession reported every failure as 'may already have been delivered', the opposite of what protocol.rs guarantees — told it might have landed, a user does not resend and the agent waits forever.
_findings.a fail-open in the plugin policy, caught: Round 3 shipped `plugins` in AgentPolicy::dimensions() but NOT in the version table, and check_daemon_understands maps an unrecognised name onto POLICY_DIMENSIONS_VERSION. Config::policy copies the field straight through, so `plugins = "none"` in agent.toml reached that path WITH NO CLI FLAG AT ALL: the check passed, the daemon dropped the key, and the session loaded every plugin and ran every SessionStart hook. Fixed in 6d3ce356 — PROTOCOL_VERSION 7->8, PLUGIN_POLICY_VERSION = 8, and the table split out as settings_a_daemon_could_drop so it can be asserted without a socket. ORCHESTRATOR CHECKED THE BLAST RADIUS: the L16's shipped /usr/bin/apex has NO plugin policy at all (0 `--plugins` flags in help, 0 string matches in the binary) and there is no agent.toml on the machine, so the fail-open lived only in unreleased branch code and never reached Andre. The live daemon answers protocol 1 and refuses --plugins outright, which is fail-closed and correct.
_findings.--plugins has never gone through the dae: The L16's daemon answers protocol 1, so `apex agent run --plugins none` is refused with 'speaks protocol 1 and would ignore --plugins' and no session starts — correct behaviour, but it means session.rs -> document wiring is unit-tested only. Closing it needs a daemon built from the tip, i.e. restarting apex-agentd or an image. THAT IS ANDRE'S CALL, not an agent's, and the standing rule forbids `pkill apex-agentd`. Also: the live plugin-removal test is #[ignore]d and ran on the L16 only — CI installs no `claude`, so CI has never held that check; the suite prints a '----' could-not-run line counted separately from PASS rather than passing vacuously.

_findings.`cargo test -p apex-remoted` does not re: Three mutations of inject.rs came back GREEN against a binary compiled before they existed — a mutation that cannot fail, in the harness rather than the Containerfile this time. This is the THIRD stale-artefact defect in two days, after check-doc-verbs.sh reading a target/debug/apex that cargo test --bins --no-run never refreshes. Whenever a test drives a BINARY rather than a library, ask what rebuilt it.
_findings.round 1 refused a criterion with arithme: P1-059 C2 was refused as impossible: MAX_PAYLOAD 65514, base64 4/3, ~48 KB against a 100 KB-2 MB screenshot. Every number correct; all of it measured a Frame::Control. Open/Data/Close IS begin/chunk/end — wire.rs:66 says so — and Frame::data_frames had been chunking every PTY byte the phone ever received. One daemon verb closed it. The lesson for every unit: before recording that something cannot be done, check which TYPE your measurement was about. A false 'cannot be done from here' is how work does not get done, and this is the second instance in two days (p2-f claimed GreetContext.qml was in apex-shell).

_ci: CI RAN FOR THE FIRST TIME IN THIS PROGRAM, and this is the record of what that cost and bought. pr-validation.yml triggered ONLY on `pull_request: branches: [main]`, and the program is forbidden from opening a PR until final integration - so sixty landed items, twelve landings and ~2000 Rust tests had been verified on exactly one laptop. `gh run list --branch roadmap/v2.2` returned nothing at all. Fixed in four commits, each one exposing the next problem: (1) push + workflow_dispatch triggers added; the first run failed in 18s. (2) The parity check cloned apex-shell's DEFAULT branch, so it compared apex-os roadmap/v2.2 against apex-shell main and reported drift on two touchpad defaults - while the two INTEGRATION branches agreed perfectly at 22 settings. It now clones the matching branch and PRINTS which one it used. THE DRIFT IT EXPOSED IS REAL AND IS KEPT: apex-shell main has drag_lock=true and click_method=clickfinger where apex-os main's generator has false and buttonAreas, so whoever does the final integration must land both sides together or opening the Input page silently changes a user's touchpad behaviour. (3) The path classifier read github.event.pull_request.* and died with exit 128 on a push; it is now event-aware and, when no range can be determined, selects EVERYTHING - this file already records four occasions where a selector picked nothing, the job skipped, and the workflow passed. (4) Six confinement assertions in mcp_sidecar_live.rs had never run anywhere but the L16 because the runner has no bubblewrap; installed rather than skipped, because they are the assertions that the sandbox IS a sandbox. Then bwrap failed on Ubuntu 24.04's kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1, so the sysctl is relaxed and PROVEN with a smoke check before any test runs. THE FINDING THAT PAYS FOR ALL OF IT: on the runner, /proc/N/cgroup reads '/system.slice/hosted-compute-agent.service', which is neither a login session nor a user service - a THIRD classification distinct from the L16's session scope and from scheduled-job. Two request_origin tests fail there while nine pass. Four rounds of orchestrators wrote that the workflow file was the only evidence of what CI presents; it is now measured, and p0-014 has been sent the exact string while it is still live.

_incident_two_orchestrators: At 03:06 the apex-roadmap-resume.timer started its OWN `claude -p` orchestrator (pid 3849364), correctly, because the 3am usage limit had killed every one of this session's agents and it saw nothing alive. It landed four branches at 03:11 (p1-061, p2-b, p1-053c, p2-a) — good work, verified green by all three gates and kept. It was about to dispatch six agents when this session came back. TWO ORCHESTRATORS IS ACTIVELY HARMFUL: both dispatch to a ceiling of six, both write this file, and both use the same worktree paths, so two agents in /var/tmp/apex-work/wt-p2-f would corrupt each other. The duplicate was terminated before it dispatched (autoresume.log: 'resume session ended (exit 143)'), so nothing was lost. ROADMAP/state/AUTORESUME was LEFT IN PLACE deliberately — the mechanism is correct and is the only rescue if this session dies; it skips while agents are alive, which is why it only fired during the window when all of them were dead. The lesson is to re-dispatch promptly after a limit so the next timer check sees live agents and skips.
